method: c3 + q34 as the 3D-shape authority (the slot back-projected from c3 onto the cylinder through the solved camera; the side panels on a mm grid for X/Z); body = one lofted solid whose sections carry the heavy rim (muzzle_brake_geo.section); slot cut by a cutter whose outer-edge round is real geometry; no bevel modifier
method_changes: iteration 1: symmetric through-slots opened the background through the face and the slot in c3 / q34 -> right side only (spec_proposal.json)

iteration 2: boolean slant cut + weighted bevel left the rim SHARP (XZ sections): Blender's clamp-overlap limit is global and a 0.036 mm boolean edge collapsed every bevel -> rim built into lofted sections
iteration 4: the unclamped weighted bevel on the slot threw vertices out (bl.bevel guard) -> slot round built into the cutter
known_differences: the detent latch reads as a thin clean plate; c3 draws a chunkier knob placed further back over the FSB (q34: at the junction)
the face and lip run ~4 mm further forward than c3 draws (pinned by the side trace, 880.0 overall)
materials: the ROUGH LOOK has no wear on the rim edges (texture stage, not design)
